record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: If f (z) = ∞ n n=1 an z is analytic in D and n=1 |an | < +∞, can f (z) map the unit circle T onto a curve of positive two-dimensional measure if (a) f (z) in S, (b) more generally, f ′ (z) 6= 0 in D?

evidence.quote: If f (z) = ∞ n n=1 an z is analytic in D and n=1 |an | < +∞, can f (z) map the unit circle T onto a curve of positive two-dimensional measure if (a) f (z) in S, (b) more generally, f ′ (z) 6= 0 in D?

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this question for either the univalent class $S$ or for locally univalent functions with absolutely convergent Taylor coefficients. Related results (e.g., Goodman's work on univalent functions and nonanalytic curves, and constructions of schlicht series with peculiar boundary convergence behavior) are known but do not appear to settle whether the image of the unit circle can have positive planar measure under the stated coefficient hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Univalent Functions and Nonanalytic Curves (Goodman, 1957)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses absolute and uniform convergence of f' on |z|=1 and the resulting smoothness of the image curve, but does not address the positive-area question under the absolute summability hypothesis.
status_evidence.claim: Related background on boundary behavior of univalent functions with absolutely convergent derivative series; does not settle the problem.

status_evidence.title: Schlicht Taylor series whose convergence on the unit circle is non-uniform
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of univalent (schlicht) Taylor series with various boundary convergence behaviors.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context for boundary pathologies of schlicht series but does not resolve the positive 2D-measure question for the image of T.
